_ssot: Decisions only. Never freeze scan results here -- `shared_skills.py report` recomputes them, so a stale hash in this file can never disagree with reality.
_rule: A skill is either shared infrastructure (exactly one copy, here, reachable from every project through the user-level surfaces) or repo-owned (differentiated on purpose, lives in that repo's big loop). Nothing is both. A repo holding its own copy of a shared name shadows the shared one silently -- that is what `check` exists to catch.

surfaces._note: Canonical is the .agents/ side, matching this machine's dominant convention and Codex's own repo skill discovery path. The .claude/ side links into it relatively, as the other 42 user-level entries already do.

shared.name: shared-skills-infra
shared.why: The governance tool has to sit under its own rule, or the one skill that can detect shadowing is the one nothing checks.

shared.name: github-delivery-loop
shared.why: Merge authority is host infrastructure, not repo policy: the same four-layer stack and the same two hosts gate every repo. It was already diverged into two versions (skill-bettor v0.1 vs ix-agy v1.1) and that divergence is exactly what made the same blockers recur.

repo_owned.name: ios-agent-autopilot
repo_owned.why: Device automation is genuinely ix-agy-specific; no other repo has the hardware surface.

repo_owned.name: subproject-ixsecurity-e2e
repo_owned.why: Named after an ix-agy subproject; not portable by construction.
